stops.stop: Vatican City, questioned about the counterfeit bonds
stops.date_confidence: Attested (Wikipedia, 'Paul Marcinkus'). The interview was conducted by United States federal prosecutors; Marcinkus was in Vatican City and the stop is pinned there rather than in the United States, since he did not travel to it. No charge followed, and the record does not say what he told them.

stops.stop: Mineola, Long Island, the Franklin National fails
stops.date_confidence: Insolvency date attested (Wikipedia, 'Michele Sindona'; TIME archive). Coordinates corrected to Mineola, where the bank's headquarters stood from 1960 until the failure; the research pool pinned Franklin Square, the village of the bank's origin (liherald.com, 'Rise and fall of Franklin National Bank'). The scale of the Vatican bank's losses is reported as tens of millions and is not precisely established. Marcinkus was not present; the stop is his because the loss is his institution's.

stops.stop: Geneva, the Vatican pays the creditors
stops.date_confidence: Date corrected and refined from the pool's '1984-05': UPI reports the accord initialled on the Sunday and signed at Geneva on Friday 25 May 1984.
